messages:
matt: Heads-up — got reproducible p95 regressions on tenant that mixes lots of tiny KV hits with occasional long LLM generations after we bumped host-offload aggressiveness. baseline ~22ms -> spike ~58ms.

rachel: Timeline? which change likely triggered it?

matt: We widened offload window + allowed more small pages to live on host to save VRAM. Problem is DMA and pin tails: many tiny pins serialized on host staging and dma queue saturated. Trace snippet: `rpc -> kvcache miss -> prefetch -> host-pin -> dma_submit -> wait`.

sunil: That matches saturation: prefetch plus tiny allocations are creating a noisy neighbor effect. What fixes have we tried?

matt: Quick fixes: 1) revert threshold (helps) 2) microbatch pin coalesce (helps most), 3) bump staging slots (helps but increases host mem).

rachel: We need a robust plan: avoid reverting while keeping VRAM wins. Proposed multi-layer approach: tokenized admission for prefetch + tiny allocations; tiny-slab fastpath to cut alloc latency; coalesce DMA; and a load-aware compaction controller.

sunil: Walk through tokens. token model must be cheap on hot path.
matt: Token idea: two token pools per tenant: tiny_slots and prefetch_outstanding. Checkout is atomic decrement; if token unavailable we fallback: tiny -> slow allocator, prefetch -> queue async or drop prefetch. Refill is adaptive based on dma_queue_util and slab_free_ratio.

rachel: Refill policy sketch: when dma_util < 30% and slab_free > 40% increase tokens; when dma_util > 70% decay tokens fast. Add short global burst allowance for transient spikes that checks host_cpu_idle.

sunil: How to persist token state across scheduler restarts? Local cache + periodic resync with control-plane. Stale tokens acceptable since refill conservatively bounds consumption.

matt: tiny-slab: preallocate per-GPU small arenas for <=512B. Lockless freelist fastpath returns slot instantly. Slabs pre-pinned to avoid madvise cost. Eviction is background: mark slab evictable, stop new allocs, compact live slots async, then unpin old slab.

rachel: Compaction risks: doing heavy compaction during peak hurts latency. Need controller that only compacts when safe. Use a PID-like controller that considers dma_queue_util, host_cpu_idle, and recent p99 tail. Target: keep dma_queue_util < 30% and host_cpu_idle > 15% before accelerating compaction.

sunil: Also need cancellation semantics: if queue climbs mid-compaction, controller should pause and rollback partial compacts safely. Rolling compactions of small chunks preferred.

matt: Microbatch coalesce remains useful — aggregate pins for concurrent microbatch requests to amortize DMA submits. Coalesce window must be small (2-8ms) to limit added latency for single-rpc flows.

rachel: Instrumentation required: dma_queue_util, host_pinning_wait_ms, slab_free_ratio, slab_reuse_rate, tenant_prefetch_outstanding, token_grants, compaction_ops, and prefetch_cancels. Dashboards and a traced span for token checkout.

sunil: Testing plan: mixed-harness with tunable prefetch aggressiveness, tiny allocation ratio, and background eviction pressure. Measure p50/p95/p99 and host mem usage. Also fault-inject: force token exhaustion, force compaction pause.

matt: Rollout plan: feature flag token admission + coalesce + tiny-slab behind flags. Start on low-traffic tenants, then noisy tenants. Observe metrics for 48h windows and be ready to revert.

rachel: Quick config prototype for experiments (just a JSON blob we used in staging):

```
{
  "tiny_slab_slot_bytes": 256,
  "tiny_slab_size_kib": 128,
  "tiny_threshold_bytes": 512,
  "prefetch_token_initial": 32,
  "tiny_token_initial": 128,
  "coalesce_window_ms": 5,
  "compaction_target_dma_util": 0.30
}
```

sunil: Good. Action items: matt prototype token checkout + kvcache hooks; rachel owns telemetry + PID spec; i'll build harness and run staging experiment and validate failure modes. ops-bot: can you open an experiment ticket?

ops-bot: Created EXP-2024-331: "evictor-prefetch-token-admission + tiny-slab + coalesce experiment" assigned [matt, rachel, sunil] priority P1.

matt: I'll open the PR for token checkout and coalesce patch and include a debug flag to force token exhaustion for repro.

rachel: I'll add dashboards and set alerts if dma_queue_util > 80% or slab_free_ratio < 10%.

sunil: Let's run a 6h soak in staging and then a 24h run on a small subset of tenants if results look good. If anything regresses, we have quick rollback knobs (disable coalesce, disable tiny-slab, revert threshold).

matt: Thanks team. Hoping this keeps the VRAM wins without the tail regressions. Will post staging numbers tomorrow. :rocket:
